intake.label: Scope
scope.none.p: The solution does not use AI when it runs, so there is no AI risk tier to assess and no AI controls to apply. Govern it like any other software:
scope.none.1: Security: review code before each release, scan dependencies and secrets, and test for common vulnerabilities.
scope.none.2: Quality: keep automated tests, and have a person review AI-generated code before it is merged.
scope.none.3: Data protection: apply your usual privacy, data-classification and hosting rules.
scope.none.4: AI coding tools: agree which tools are allowed, and what code or data may be shared with them.
scope.none.ref: A widely used reference for secure development is the NIST Secure Software Development Framework:
scope.none.again: If an AI feature is added later, change this answer to Yes and assess it.

prio.title: Prioritisation for AI
prio.intro: Three questions from the UAE government's AI-assistant priority matrix. They don't change the risk tier; they recommend how much autonomy the AI should have.
prio.notrisk: These are not risk questions. Describe the service as it is today; there is no safe or unsafe answer.
auto.title: Recommended autonomy
auto.pending: Answer the three prioritisation questions in the deep-dive to get a recommended autonomy level.
auto.l1.desc: The AI runs the service end to end, with little routine human involvement. Suits high-usage, low-complexity services with high readiness.
auto.l2.desc: The AI carries out most steps; people handle exceptions and approvals. Suits medium-complexity services, or services whose readiness is not yet high.
auto.l3.desc: The AI recommends or prepares the work, and people keep every decision. Suits low-readiness settings and early adoption.
auto.l4.desc: Usage is low or the service is highly complex, so AI should not be applied yet. Simplify the process or build readiness first.
auto.scale: Levels are numbered as in the UAE priority matrix: 1 is full autonomous execution and 4 is not suitable yet. A lower number means more autonomy.
auto.cap.tier-high: Capped at level 2, supervised autonomy, because the risk tier is High.
auto.cap.regulated: Capped at level 2, supervised autonomy, because the service is in a regulated domain.
auto.exceeds: Warning: as designed, it acts at level {n}, which is more autonomous than recommended. Reduce its autonomy or improve readiness first.
auto.exceeds.l4: Warning: as designed, it uses AI at level {n}, but this service is not suitable for AI yet.
auto.cap.tier-unacceptable: The use is prohibited, so no AI autonomy is appropriate.
auto.fits: As designed (level {n}), it stays within the recommendation.
sc.auto: Separate from the risk tier, three prioritisation questions (usage, complexity, readiness) give a recommended autonomy level. They follow the UAE government's AI-assistant priority matrix and its numbering, where level 1 is full autonomous execution and level 4 is not suitable yet. Low usage or high complexity gives level 4. Otherwise readiness decides: high readiness gives level 1 for a high-usage, low-complexity service and level 2 for the rest, medium readiness gives level 2, and low readiness gives level 3. A High tier or a regulated domain never allows level 1. If the AI as designed acts more autonomously than recommended, the kit warns you.

gd.title: User guide
gd.intro: Everything you need to assess an AI use case with this kit. The first one takes about ten minutes. There is nothing to install, download or upload.
gd.s1.h: 1. Assess a use case in three steps
gd.s1.1: Add a use case. On the home page, choose Start your first assessment. Give the use case a name and an accountable owner; the other details are optional.
gd.s1.2: Answer the quick check. Eight multiple-choice questions about impact, data, who is affected, the type of AI, autonomy, oversight, access and reversibility. Each answer shows the points it adds.
gd.s1.3: Read the result. You get a risk tier with the reasons behind it, then the controls that apply under the frameworks you selected, then the exports.
gd.s1.deep: For a fuller picture, complete the deep-dive: ten more questions plus three optional prioritisation questions. The deep-dive can raise the tier but never lower it. Complete it before any High-risk use case goes to committee.
gd.s1.fw: Choose the frameworks you follow on the home page. The control list and the exports only show references to those frameworks.
gd.fig.home: The home page: three steps and one button to start.
gd.fig.quick: The quick check: eight questions, about two minutes.
gd.fig.tier: The result: a tier, the top reasons and the full points breakdown.
gd.s2.intro: The tier is the higher of two results: the points from your answers, and any named rule that sets a minimum tier. How scoring works lists every weight.
gd.t.little: Under 20 points. Keep it on the register and apply the baseline controls the kit lists.
gd.t.limited: 20 to 44 points. More controls apply; review them with the accountable owner before launch.
gd.t.high: 45 points or more, or a named rule applies (for example, the AI makes decisions about people without a person approving each one). The full control set applies. Complete the deep-dive and take the committee report to your risk committee before launch.
gd.t.unacceptable: Only through a rule, for prohibited uses such as social scoring. Do not proceed; escalate to your risk committee and legal team.
gd.s3.p1: Controls are grouped by theme: accountability, transparency, data, human oversight, safety and security, and monitoring. Each one says what to do in plain words.
gd.s3.p2: The grey chips are references: the clause, article or principle in each selected framework that asks for the control. ISO/IEC 42001 is cited by clause number only. The numbered links under a control are the official sources used to check it.
gd.s3.badges: Every control carries a verification badge:
gd.s3.v: its references were checked against the cited official sources.
gd.s3.n: the control is sound, but at least one reference has not been checked yet. Hover over the badge to see why, and confirm the reference before you rely on it.
gd.s3.filter: Use the filters to show one framework, or verified controls only.
gd.fig.controls: Controls grouped by theme, with references and verification badges.
gd.s4.p1: The three prioritisation questions at the end of the deep-dive (usage, complexity and readiness) recommend how much autonomy the AI should have, from level 1 (full autonomous execution) to level 4 (not suitable for AI yet). The levels are numbered as in the UAE government's AI-assistant priority matrix, so a lower number means more autonomy. They do not change the risk tier.
gd.s4.p2: A High tier or a regulated domain never allows level 1: the recommendation stops at level 2, supervised autonomy. If the AI as designed acts more autonomously than recommended, the kit shows a warning: reduce its autonomy or improve readiness first.
gd.s5.pdf: Committee report. On the Export step, choose Committee PDF. Your print dialog opens; choose Save as PDF. The one-to-two-page summary has the tier, the reasons, the control checklist and a sign-off block.
gd.s5.ctl: Control lists. Download the controls as XLSX or CSV to track them in a spreadsheet. Arabic sheets open right to left.
gd.s5.backup: Back up your register. On the home page, open Save or restore and choose Save a backup (.json). Do this regularly: clearing your browser data deletes the register.
gd.s5.share: Share or move it. Send the .json file to a colleague. They open the kit, choose Save or restore, then Restore a saved register (.json), and can replace or merge their own. For a read-only overview, use Export register (XLSX).
gd.s5.tpl: Prefer spreadsheets? The Templates page has the register, impact assessment and control checklist to fill in offline. You don't need them to use the kit.
gd.fig.export: The Export step: the committee PDF, and the controls as XLSX or CSV.
gd.s6.p: The kit has no server. Your use cases are stored only in this browser and are never sent anywhere; you can confirm this in your browser's network tools. Other people cannot see them, and neither can other browsers on your computer. In a private window, or where storage is blocked, the kit warns you that changes will be lost when you close the page, so save a backup.
gd.s6.clear: To remove everything, choose Clear all data under the register.
